1.text: Now it happened in tha days when tha judges ruled, dat there was a famine in tha land. N a certain man of Beth-lehem-judah went 2 stay in tha country of Moab, he, N his wife, N his two sons.
N tha name of tha man was Elimelech, N tha name of his wife Naomi, N tha name of his two sons Mahlon N Chilion, Ephrathites of Beth-lehem-judah. N dey came in2 tha country of Moab, N continued there.
N Elimelech Naomi’s husband died; N she was left, N her two sons.
N dey took ’em wives of tha women of Moab; tha name of tha one was Orpah, N tha name of tha other Ruth: N dey dwelled there about ten years.
N Mahlon N Chilion died also both of ’em; N tha woman was left of her two sons N her husband.
Then she arose wit her daughters in law, dat she might return from tha country of Moab: 4 she had heard in tha country of Moab how dat tha LORD had visited his people in givin ’em bread.
So she went forth out of tha place where she was, N her two daughters in law wit her; N dey went on tha way 2 return 2 tha land of Judah.
N Naomi said 2 her two daughters in law, Go, return each 2 her mother’s house: tha LORD deal kindly wit u, as y’all have dealt wit tha dead, N wit me.
Tha LORD grant u dat y’all may find rest, each of u in tha house of her husband. Then she kissed ’em; N dey lifted up their voice, N wept.
N dey said 2 her, Surely we will return wit u 2 ur people.
N Naomi said, Turn again, my daughters: why will y’all go wit me? r there yet any more sons in my womb, dat dey may be ur husbands?
Turn again, my daughters, go ur way; 4 I am too old 2 have an husband. If I should say, I have hope, if I should have an husband also 2 night, N should also bear sons;
Would y’all tarry 4 ’em till dey were grown? would y’all stay 4 ’em from havin husbands? no, my daughters; 4 it grieveth me much 4 ur sakes dat tha hand of tha LORD is gone out against me.
N dey lifted up their voice, N wept again: N Orpah kissed her mother in law; but Ruth clave 2 her.
N she said, look, ur sister in law is gone back 2 her people, N 2 her gods: return u after ur sister in law.
N Ruth said, Intreat me not 2 leave u, or 2 return from followin after u: 4 where u go, I will go; N where u lodgest, I will lodge: ur people shall be my people, N ur God my God:
Where u die, will I die, N there will I be buried: tha LORD do so 2 me, N more also, if ought but death part u N me.
When she saw dat she was stedfastly minded 2 go wit her, then she left speakin 2 her.
So dey two went until dey came 2 Beth-lehem. N it happened, when dey were come 2 Beth-lehem, dat all tha city was moved about ’em, N dey said, Is dis Naomi?
N she said 2 ’em, Call me not Naomi, call me Mara: 4 tha Almighty has dealt very bitterly wit me.
I went out full, N tha LORD has brought me home again empty: why then call y’all me Naomi, seein tha LORD has testified against me, N tha Almighty has afflicted me?
So Naomi returned, N Ruth tha Moabitess, her daughter in law, wit her, which returned out of tha country of Moab: N dey came 2 Beth-lehem in tha beginning of barley harvest.

2.text: N Naomi had a kinsman of her husband’s, a mighty man of wealth, of tha family of Elimelech; N his name was Boaz.
N Ruth tha Moabitess said 2 Naomi, Let me now go 2 tha field, N glean ears of corn after him in whose sight I shall find grace. N she said 2 her, Go, my daughter.
N she went, N came, N gleaned in tha field after tha reapers: N her hap was 2 light on a part of tha field belonging 2 Boaz, who was of tha kindred of Elimelech.
N, look, Boaz came from Beth-lehem, N said 2 tha reapers, tha LORD be wit u. N dey answered him, tha LORD bless u.
Then said Boaz 2 his servant dat was set over tha reapers, Whose damsel is dis?
N tha servant dat was set over tha reapers answered, It is tha Moabitish damsel dat came back wit Naomi out of tha country of Moab:
N she said, I pray u, let me glean N gather after tha reapers among tha sheaves: so she came, N has continued even from tha morning until now, dat she tarried a little in tha house.
Then said Boaz 2 Ruth, hear u not, my daughter? Go not 2 glean in another field, neither go from hence, but abide here fast by my maidens:

Let ur eyes be on tha field dat dey do reap, N go u after ’em: have I not charged tha young men dat dey shall not touch u? N when u r athirst, go 2 tha vessels, N drink of dat which tha young men have drawn.
Then she fell on her face, N bowed herself 2 tha ground, N said 2 him, Why have I found grace in ur eyes, dat u should take knowledge of me, seein I am a stranger?

N Boaz answered 2 her, It has fully been showed me, all dat u have done 2 ur mother in law since tha death of thine husband: N how u have left ur father N ur mother, N tha land of ur nativity, N art come 2 a people which u knew not before now.
Tha LORD recompense ur work, N a full reward be given u of tha LORD God of Israel, under whose wings u r come 2 trust.
Then she said, Let me find favour in ur sight, my lord; 4 dat u have comforted me, N 4 dat u have spoken friendly 2 thine handmaid, though I don’t be like 2 one of thine handmaidens.
N Boaz said 2 her, At mealtime come u here, N eat of tha bread, N dip ur morsel in tha vinegar. N she sat beside tha reapers: N he reached her parched corn, N she did eat, N was sufficed, N left.
N when she was risen up 2 glean, Boaz commanded his young men, sayin, Let her glean even among tha sheaves, N reproach her not:
N let fall also some of tha handfuls of purpose 4 her, N leave ’em, dat she may glean ’em, N rebuke her not.
So she gleaned in tha field until even, N beat out dat she had gleaned: N it was about an ephah of barley.
N she took it up, N went in2 tha city: N her mother in law saw what she had gleaned: N she brought forth, N gave 2 her dat she had reserved after she was sufficed.

N her mother in law said 2 her, Where have u gleaned 2 day? N where wroughtest u? blessed be he dat did take knowledge of u. N she showed her mother in law wit whom she had wrought, N said, tha man’s name wit whom I wrought 2 day is Boaz.
N Naomi said 2 her daughter in law, Blessed be he of tha LORD, who has not left off his kindness 2 tha livin N 2 tha dead. N Naomi said 2 her, tha man is near of kin 2 us, one of our next kinsmen.
N Ruth tha Moabitess said, He said 2 me also, u will keep fast by my young men, until dey have ended all my harvest.
N Naomi said 2 Ruth her daughter in law, It is good, my daughter, dat u go out wit his maidens, dat dey meet u not in any other field.
So she kept fast by tha maidens of Boaz 2 glean 2 tha end of barley harvest N of wheat harvest; N lived wit her mother in law.

3.text: Then Naomi her mother in law said 2 her, My daughter, shall I not seek rest 4 u, dat it may be well wit u?
N now is not Boaz of our kindred, wit whose maidens u were? look, he winnoweth barley 2 night in tha threshingfloor.
Wash urself therefore, N anoint u, N put ur clothing upon u, N get u down 2 tha floor: but make not urself known 2 tha man, until he shall have done eatin N drinkin.
N it will be, when he lies down, dat u will mark tha place where he shall lie, N u will go in, N uncover his feet, N lay u down; N he will tell u what u will do.
N she said 2 her, All dat u sayest 2 me I will do.
N she went down 2 tha floor, N did according 2 all dat her mother in law told her.
N when Boaz had eaten N drunk, N his heart was merry, he went 2 lie down at tha end of tha heap of corn: N she came softly, N uncovered his feet, N laid her down.
N it happened at midnight, dat tha man was afraid, N turned himself: N, look, a woman lay at his feet.
N he said, Who r u? N she answered, I am Ruth thine handmaid: spread therefore ur skirt over thine handmaid; 4 u r a near kinsman.
N he said, Blessed be u of tha LORD, my daughter: 4 u have showed more kindness in tha latter end than at tha beginning, since as u followedst not young men, whether poor or rich.
N now, my daughter, don’t fear; I will do 2 u all dat u requirest: 4 all tha city of my people does know dat u r a virtuous woman.
N now it is true dat I am ur near kinsman: but there is a kinsman nearer than I.

Tarry dis night, N it will be in tha morning, dat if he will perform 2 u tha part of a kinsman, well; let him do tha kinsman’s part: but if he will not do tha part of a kinsman 2 u, then will I do tha part of a kinsman 2 u, as tha LORD lives: lie down until tha morning.
N she lay at his feet until tha morning: N she rose up before one could know another. N he said, Let it not be known dat a woman came in2 tha floor.
Also he said, Bring tha vail dat u have upon u, N hold it. N when she held it, he measured six measures of barley, N laid it on her: N she went in2 tha city.
N when she came 2 her mother in law, she said, Who r u, my daughter? N she told her all dat tha man had done 2 her.
N she said, dese six measures of barley gave he me; 4 he said 2 me, Go not empty 2 ur mother in law.
Then said she, Sit still, my daughter, until u know how tha matter will fall: 4 tha man will not be in rest, until he have finished tha thing dis day.

4.text: Then went Boaz up 2 tha gate, N sat him down there: N, look, tha kinsman of whom Boaz spoke came by; 2 whom he said, Ho, such a one! turn aside, sit down here. N he turned aside, N sat down.
N he took ten men of tha elders of tha city, N said, Sit y’all down here. N dey sat down.
N he said 2 tha kinsman, Naomi, dat is come again out of tha country of Moab, sells a parcel of land, which was our brother Elimelech’s:

N I thought 2 advertise u, sayin, Buy it before tha inhabitants, N before tha elders of my people. If u will redeem it, redeem it: but if u will not redeem it, then tell me, dat I may know: 4 there is none 2 redeem it beside u; N I am after u. N he said, I will redeem it.
Then said Boaz, What day u buyest tha field of tha hand of Naomi, u must buy it also of Ruth tha Moabitess, tha wife of tha dead, 2 raise up tha name of tha dead upon his inheritance.
N tha kinsman said, I cannot redeem it 4 myself, lest I mar my own inheritance: redeem u my right 2 urself; 4 I cannot redeem it.

Now dis was tha manner in former time in Israel concerning redeeming N concerning changing, 4 2 confirm all things; a man plucked off his shoe, N gave it 2 his neighbour: N dis was a testimony in Israel.
Therefore tha kinsman said 2 Boaz, Buy it 4 u. So he drew off his shoe.
N Boaz said 2 tha elders, N 2 all tha people, y’all r witnesses dis day, dat I have bought all dat was Elimelech’s, N all dat was Chilion’s N Mahlon’s, of tha hand of Naomi.

Moreover Ruth tha Moabitess, tha wife of Mahlon, have I purchased 2 be my wife, 2 raise up tha name of tha dead upon his inheritance, dat tha name of tha dead don’t be cut off from among his brothers, N from tha gate of his place: y’all r witnesses dis day.

N all tha people dat were in tha gate, N tha elders, said, We r witnesses. tha LORD make tha woman dat is come in2 thine house like Rachel N like Leah, which two did build tha house of Israel: N do u worthily in Ephratah, N be famous in Beth-lehem:
N let ur house be like tha house of Pharez, whom Tamar bare 2 Judah, of tha seed which tha LORD shall give u of dis young woman.
So Boaz took Ruth, N she was his wife: N when he went in 2 her, tha LORD gave her conception, N she bare a son.
N tha women said 2 Naomi, Blessed be tha LORD, which has not left u dis day without a kinsman, dat his name may be famous in Israel.
N he shall be 2 u a restorer of ur life, N a nourisher of thine old age: 4 ur daughter in law, which loves u, which is better 2 u than seven sons, has born him.
N Naomi took tha child, N laid it in her bosom, N became nurse 2 it.
N tha women her neighbours gave it a name, sayin, There is a son born 2 Naomi; N dey called his name Obed: he is tha father of Jesse, tha father of David.
Now dese r tha generations of Pharez: Pharez fathered Hezron,
N Hezron fathered Ram, N Ram fathered Amminadab,
N Amminadab fathered Nahshon, N Nahshon fathered Salmon,
N Salmon fathered Boaz, N Boaz fathered Obed,
N Obed fathered Jesse, N Jesse fathered David.
